comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Evidence pass over all 12 failed Reconcile Bridge runs (2026-08-06 -> 2026-08-11). The Mode 2 framing in the description is REFUTED; Mode 1 is confirmed.

MODE 1 — CONFIRMED, 6/12 runs terminating (31481490100, 31358521998, 31350775907, 31263067299, 31222668500, 31179770156). Identical in all six: fails on the VERY FIRST ACLI call (jira workitem search --jql ...), 15-20s after 'Reconciling in/with mode: live', with NO reconcile work preceding it. The 'acli jira auth login' step earlier in the job SUCCEEDED (cache hit acli-Linux-1.3.19-stable, no login error). So the token is rejected at FIRST USE, not at login — i.e. the JIRA_API_TOKEN secret value is expired/revoked, not a session dying mid-pass.

MODE 2 — REFUTED as a failure cause, 0/12 runs terminating. 'command cancelled' is non-fatal stderr NOISE inside the outbound link-apply loop. It first appears right after 'RECON: typed_inbound_dispatched count=16' (or 19), 2-6 min in, and each occurrence is bracketed by a SUCCESSFUL 'RECON: batch_outcome action=update key=REB-... error=None links_applied=N'. No exit code, no HTTP status, no traceback, no reconciler-level ERROR attached. The enclosing operation is recorded as succeeding.

The 6 runs the sweep attributed to Mode 2 actually died in GIT DELIVERY, in three unrelated classes:
  - TLS: 'server certificate verification failed. CAfile: none CRLfile: none' (31535962079 push-transport-failed, 3 unpushed commits; 31420498173 merge-recovery-blocked, 2 unpushed)
  - Ref push rejected: 31455622724 stale --force-with-lease on refs/reconciler/last-pass; 31244501098 lost race on refs/heads/tickets ('is at e45f61a9 but expected 9ecaaa40', 6 unpushed)
  - Re-dispatch: 31129551929 + 31129431096, 'HTTP 422: Cannot trigger a workflow_dispatch on a disabled workflow'

AC3 ANSWERED, opposite to the hypothesis: Mode 1 and Mode 2 are INDEPENDENT. 'unauthorized' count is 0 in all six Mode-2-noise runs; the two signatures never co-occur. Mode 2 is not the expiry surfacing mid-pass.

AC4 is MOOT: no pass is aborted by Mode 2, so there is no partially-applied reconcile from that cause.

CODE DEFECT FOUND for Mode 1 reporting, in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py: the auth fast-abort is keyed on '_AUTH_FAILURE_CODE = 401' / 'if cpe.returncode == _AUTH_FAILURE_CODE'. ACLI is a subprocess and exits 1, never 401, so that branch is DEAD CODE. An expired credential is therefore retried 3x with backoff (pointless — it is deterministic) and then surfaces as the generic 'reconcile_once raised: ... returned non-zero exit status 1'. Nothing in rebar_reconciler/ matches the 'unauthorized' / 'auth login' stderr string.

SCOPE DECISION. AC1's RENEWAL half is not achievable in code: since the token is rejected at first use, re-running 'acli jira auth login' with the same JIRA_API_TOKEN cannot help. Renewal requires ROTATING the secret — an ops action needing a new secret value, deliberately not attempted here. This ticket will deliver the detection/reporting half (AC2) as a self-contained fix; the git-delivery failures and the swallowed 'command cancelled' noise will be filed as separate linked tickets.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIX PUSHED — Gerrit change 1640 'Fast-abort ACLI auth failure on stderr marker', awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

WHAT CHANGED (2 source files, 1 new test file, +279/-3):

1. src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py
   - Added _AUTH_FAILURE_MARKERS + _is_auth_failure(stderr): detects credential rejection where ACLI actually reports it (stderr), matched case-insensitively. Kept deliberately TIGHT — credential-rejection wording only ('unauthorized', 'auth login', 'authentication failed', 'invalid credentials'), NOT authorization/permission wording ('forbidden', 'cannot be assigned'), so a data/permission fault is never reported to an operator as an expired credential.
   - Added typed AcliAuthError(RuntimeError) carrying cmd + stderr, chaining the CalledProcessError per PEP 3134. Subclasses RuntimeError so existing 'except RuntimeError' sites in the acli path are unaffected.
   - The retry loop now fast-aborts on the FIRST attempt via stderr marker OR the legacy 401 exit code (the 401 check is retained so a future ACLI that does propagate the status still fast-aborts).

2. src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py
   - _reconcile_exception_result classifies AcliAuthError as INVALID_INVOCATION (canonical exit 2) rather than OPERATIONAL_FAILURE (exit 1), with details['error_class']='auth_failed' and a message naming JIRA_API_TOKEN as the secret to rotate. Matched by TYPE NAME, not isinstance, to preserve that function's adapter-neutral posture (it must not import the Jira/ACLI adapter to classify a pass).

3. tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_acli_auth_failure.py — 19 tests.

REGRESSION COVERAGE VERIFIED, not change-detector: I ran the new tests against the pre-fix behaviour (markers emptied, so exit-code-only detection). Old code retried 3 times and raised a generic CalledProcessError — the fast-abort and typed-error tests genuinely fail against it.

GATES: make lint PASS; make typecheck PASS (mypy, 504 source files); full tests/unit/rebar_reconciler suite 2401 passed. Both touched files remain under the 800-LOC module-size cap (acli_subprocess.py 526, __main__.py 750).

AC STATUS:
- AC 'detected from stderr not a 401 exit' — MET (test asserts the verbatim failed-run stderr with returncode=1 is recognised).
- AC 'aborts on first attempt' — MET (test asserts exactly 1 spawn; was 3).
- AC 'distinct typed error' — MET.
- AC 'operator-facing message names the credential' — MET (INVALID_INVOCATION, exit 2, message names JIRA_API_TOKEN; asserts the generic 'reconcile_once raised' phrasing is absent).
- AC 'non-auth failures keep retry behaviour' — MET (regression test: 3 attempts, backoff [2,4]).
- AC 'Mode 1/Mode 2 relationship recorded' — MET (prior comment: independent).
- AC 'misattributed faults filed as linked tickets' — MET, 4 filed and linked discovered_from: subzero-locustal-junebug (TLS cert verification), freeborn-dizzy-raven (rejected ref pushes), callous-wavy-kite (422 disabled-workflow re-dispatch), satisfied-emerald-grayling (swallowed 'command cancelled' noise).
- AC 'lint/typecheck/tests pass' — MET.

STILL REQUIRES AN OPERATOR ACTION, NOT SHIPPABLE IN CODE: the JIRA_API_TOKEN secret is genuinely expired/revoked. This change makes that legible in one line instead of a generic red run, but the bridge will keep failing Mode 1 until the secret is ROTATED. Rotating it needs a new secret value and is outside what this ticket can deliver.

NOTED, NOT FIXED (deliberate scope discipline): dispatch_one.py:790 has a best-effort 'except Exception' around link ops that would swallow an AcliAuthError raised mid-link-apply as non-fatal. That is not a regression (the old CalledProcessError was swallowed there too, and worse — counted as links_applied), and the observed failures all occur on the first search call, well before link ops. Flagged here rather than widened into this change.

compiled_state.description:
## Impact, stated first

The scheduled **Reconcile Bridge** workflow failed 12 times in 6 days. An evidence pass over
all 12 failed runs (see the pinned comment) split them cleanly: **6 runs died on an ACLI
authentication failure**, and 6 died on **git delivery** faults that the original sweep
misattributed to ACLI. When the bridge stalls, only the Reconciler Heartbeat Canary notices.

This ticket now covers **the ACLI auth failure and how it is reported**. The other faults are
filed as separate linked tickets — they are unrelated causes in a different subsystem.

## Confirmed signature (6/12 runs)

Runs 31481490100, 31358521998, 31350775907, 31263067299, 31222668500, 31179770156. Identical:

    ACLI stderr: ✗ Error: unauthorized: use `acli [product] auth login` to authenticate
    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: Command `[acli, jira, workitem, search, --jql, ...]`
        returned non-zero exit status 1
    Reconcile failed (exit 1)

It fails on the **very first** ACLI call, 15–20s in, with no reconcile work preceding it. The
`acli jira auth login` workflow step **succeeded** earlier in the same job. So the token is
rejected **at first use, not at login**.

## The code defect this ticket fixes

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py` fast-aborts on auth via:

    _AUTH_FAILURE_CODE: int = 401
    ...
    if cpe.returncode == _AUTH_FAILURE_CODE:
        raise cpe

ACLI is a **subprocess** and exits **1**, never 401 — that branch is **dead code**. So a
deterministic auth failure:

1. burns the full 3-attempt retry budget with 2s+4s backoff, and
2. surfaces as the generic `reconcile_once raised: ... exit status 1`, indistinguishable from
   a data/operational failure.

Nothing in `rebar_reconciler/` matches the `unauthorized` / `auth login` stderr string.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (and why)

**Automatic credential renewal.** The token is rejected at first use, so re-running
`acli jira auth login` with the same `JIRA_API_TOKEN` cannot succeed. Renewal requires
**rotating the secret value** — an ops action needing a new secret, not a code change. No new
auth flow is invented and no credential is stored anywhere new. Rotation is flagged to the
operator, not automated here.

**The git-delivery failures** (TLS `server certificate verification failed`; rejected ref
pushes on `refs/reconciler/last-pass` and `refs/heads/tickets`; `HTTP 422` re-dispatch onto a
disabled workflow) and **the swallowed `command cancelled` noise** in the link-apply loop are
filed as separate linked tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An ACLI failure whose stderr carries an authentication/authorization marker (the
      `unauthorized` / ``use `acli ... auth login` `` text) is detected **from stderr**, not from
      a subprocess exit code of 401 that ACLI never returns. Unit test asserts a
      `CalledProcessError` with `returncode=1` + that stderr is recognised as an auth failure.
- [ ] Such a failure **aborts on the first attempt** without consuming the retry budget —
      retrying a rejected credential is deterministic and cannot succeed. Unit test asserts the
      subprocess was invoked exactly **once** (today: 3 times).
- [ ] The failure raises a **distinct typed error** (not a bare `CalledProcessError`) carrying
      the failing command, so callers can `except` it specifically. Unit test asserts the type.
- [ ] A pass failing this way emits an **operator-facing message that names the credential as
      the cause**, distinguishable from the generic `reconcile_once raised: ...` used for
      data/operational failures — so a credential problem is tellable from a data problem
      without opening the log. Unit test asserts the classifier's message/disposition.
- [ ] **Non-auth** ACLI failures keep their existing retry-and-backoff behaviour unchanged.
      Regression test asserts a non-auth non-zero exit still makes 3 attempts.
- [ ] The Mode 1 / Mode 2 relationship is **determined and recorded** on this ticket: they are
      independent (`unauthorized` count is 0 in all six `command cancelled` runs; the two
      signatures never co-occur). Recorded in the evidence comment.
- [ ] The misattributed git-delivery faults and the swallowed `command cancelled` noise exist as
      **separate tickets linked `discovered_from`** this one.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the reconciler test suite pass.

## Notes

Originally filed by an automated ops error sweep, which hypothesised that `command cancelled`
was a mid-pass abort caused by the credential expiring. The evidence pass **refuted** that: the
string is non-fatal noise bracketed by successful `batch_outcome ... error=None` lines, and those
runs actually failed in git delivery. The original AC about a "partially-applied reconcile" left
by such an abort is therefore **moot** — no pass is aborted by that string.

file_impact.reason: Replace the dead returncode==401 auth fast-abort with stderr-marker detection; raise a distinct typed auth error without consuming the retry budget
Classify the typed auth error into a distinguishable operator-facing pass result instead of the generic reconcile_once-raised message
